arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Fri: he held his thumb over her name and didn't send (Shabbat). Sat after havdalah: he sends the Moshe photo with one true sentence; she answers in under a minute ('you made my Saturday'), then asks if he'd ever leave Tel Aviv. He doesn't answer yet.
arcs.secret: Dana has been offered a job running a new cafe in Haifa from January and must answer by Mon Dec 7. She has not told Ishai.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Fri: payment date 'December 8th, in the system', then 'tell Ofer Monday' behind his hand ('printers'); a text at candle time about vector layers. Sat night: an email, the chickpea in Hanukkah colours too, 'we'll settle everything together'.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Fri: came by at lunch with pita and too much energy, hung up on him at three, cancelled Shabbat dinner by text six minutes before candles. Sat: a cheery text with six exclamation marks; Tomer tells Ishai to ask her what 'not ready' means.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Lesson 2 done Thu Nov 12. The notebook: 'I want to talk to Dana' and 'I want a date (payment kind)'. Lesson 3 Thu Nov 19.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi's cough
arcs.stage: Fri: three teas (lemon, honey, ginger), soup and challah at his Shabbat table, 'Eli's battery died', read his notebook: 'send the photo, not sorry'. Sat: Tomer hears the cough from the entrance: 'that's a chest, not weather'.
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Thu: Ishai overheard 'Double? From January? Thirty years I'm here...'; Avi said chickpeas and lost his proverb. Ishai paid full price.
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Thu: the 'hypothetical' about someone you like leaving town. Not seen Fri-Sat (Shabbat). Next: hints at the cafe next week.
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Sat: picks up the blue controller, reads Noa's text before Ishai does, asks too many questions about her ('I sat behind her in fourth grade') and tells Ishai to ask her. Next: the Pump House gallery night Wed Nov 18.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: Mr. Zelig's bench
arcs.stage: Sat: one true sentence for the photo; Dana sat on his bench Thursday 'looking at her phone like it was the sea... not this sea'. 1971: 'I stayed.'

beats.goal: Slow Shabbat morning walk with Falafel. Mr. Zelig feeds the pigeons on the bench by the pond (one he calls Herzl). Ishai asks what to write with a photo of a plant; Zelig guesses it's for a woman, tells him a photo is a letter with no words and to write one true sentence. Zelig says the coffee girl sat on his bench Thursday looking at her phone 'like it was the sea... not this sea'. Ishai doesn't understand. Never say Haifa.
beats.teaser: Mr. Zelig gives Ishai one true sentence for Dana's photo
beats.forceText: Shabbat morning in the park: Mr. Zelig tells Ishai to write one true sentence with the photo.

forceLines.say: A photo is a letter with no words. Very rude. Write one true sentence.
One sentence. Not 'sorry'. I've been told.

forceCommentary.say: A pigeon named Herzl. Finally, a cast member with ambition.

moments.text: Shabbat morning, the park almost empty. Mr. Zelig on the bench by the pond tears pita for the pigeons and talks to them by name; Falafel sits very politely at the end of his leash.

lines.say: Shabbat shalom, dog. Not you, the dog. You I haven't decided.
Shabbat shalom, Mr. Zelig. He's Falafel. He's very polite with pigeons.
Polite! He's counting them. Like a tax man.
Can I sit? I have a question. A small one.
Small questions are the expensive ones. Sit. Herzl, move over.
You named a pigeon Herzl?
He thinks he founded the bench. Ask.
If you send someone a photo of a plant. Do you write something with it?
A photo of a plant. To a woman.
I didn't say a woman.
You didn't have to. Your ears said it.

commentary.say: Even the pigeon man knows. Ishai, the whole city is in your group chat.
A pigeon named Herzl. Finally, a cast member with ambition.

moments.text: Mr. Zelig scatters the last crumbs and the pigeons rush in. He points at them one by one while he talks; Ishai listens with his elbows on his knees.

lines.say: A photo is a letter with no words. Very rude. Write one true sentence.
One. Okay. Not 'sorry'. I've been told.
Who told you? A wise person.
My neighbour. Over soup.
Soup people are always right. What is true about the plant?
He almost died. Now he's showing off. A new leaf every day.
There. That's the sentence. It's also about you. Don't tell her.
It's about the basil, Mr. Zelig.
Everything is about the basil until it isn't.
I'm writing that down. Not for her. For me.

commentary.say: 'Everything is about the basil until it isn't.' Moshe, cover your leaves.
One true sentence. Ishai's personal record is half of one.

moments.text: Ishai stands to go and Falafel tugs toward the path. Mr. Zelig stays on the bench, looking past the pond toward the street.

lines.say: Thank you, Mr. Zelig. Come on, Falafel. Leave Herzl alone.
Your coffee girl. She sat here Thursday, on her break. On my bench.
Dana? Here? She never said.
She looked at her phone like it was the sea. A long time.
Well, the sea is right there. Ten minutes' walk.
Not this sea. Another one. I know that look. I had it in 1971.
What happened in 1971?
I stayed. Go. Write your sentence. Herzl is hungry again.
Shabbat shalom, Mr. Zelig.
Shabbat shalom, tax man. Not you. The dog.

commentary.say: 'Not this sea.' Zelig, you cryptic old pigeon, what do you KNOW?
1971. I need that episode. With subtitles.

update.memory: Ishai sat with me on Shabbat. A photo of a plant for the coffee girl. I gave him one true sentence. He didn't hear the sea part.

beats.goal: Tomer drops by on Shabbat afternoon for the old blue PlayStation controller (his cousin's kid is visiting). He heard Mrs. Levi coughing from the entrance ('that's a chest, not weather'). Noa texts Ishai a too-cheerful apology with six exclamation marks; Tomer reads it first, asks too many questions about her ('I sat behind her in fourth grade') and tells Ishai to ask her what 'not ready' means. Tomer never says he likes her.
beats.teaser: Tomer comes for the blue controller and reads Noa's text first
beats.forceText: Tomer picks up the old controller; a cheery text from Noa arrives and Tomer tells Ishai to ask her what's wrong.

forceLines.say: She cancelled again? Ask her what 'not ready' means. You. Not me.
Six exclamation marks. Noa uses one a year.

forceCommentary.say: Tomer read that text faster than Ishai did. Interesting.

moments.text: A knock: Tomer in a hoodie, a bag of sunflower seeds in his fist. Ishai takes the old blue controller out of the desk drawer and Tomer inspects it like a fuse box.

lines.say: The legend. The blue one. This D-pad is still sticky from 2009.
That's your Bamba. You never cleaned it.
Evidence of a great childhood. My cousin's kid won't know what hit him.
You're going to lose to a ten-year-old on purpose?
On purpose. Sure. Write that down.
Did you hear Mrs. Levi on the stairs? Still coughing.
Heard her from the entrance. That's not weather, that's a chest.
She says weather. I made her tea three times.
Tea is good. A doctor is better. I'll tell Moti to nag her.
Moti nags everyone. She won't even notice.

commentary.say: A controller handover. The most tension in this flat since the basil sunburn.
Tomer wants a doctor for Mrs. Levi. Electrician with a heart. Rare model.

moments.text: Ishai's phone lights up on the counter: Noa. Tomer leans over and reads it before Ishai can pick it up.

message.say: Sorry about last night!!! Crazy week, crazy studio, ALL GOOD!!! Send Dana the photo or I disown you!!!

lines.say: Three exclamation marks. Twice. Noa uses one a year.
She cancelled on you again? Friday too?
Six minutes before candles. I had two challahs.
And Thursday she ran out of the bar. Did she say anything?
She said 'not ready'. At my door. At ten at night.
Not ready for what?
I don't know. She left before I could ask.
So ask. You. Not me. She tells you things.
Why not you? You've known her as long as I have.
Longer. I sat behind her in fourth grade. Anyway. Ask her.

commentary.say: Tomer, sweetie, you read that text faster than Ishai did. Interesting.
Six exclamation marks. Professionally speaking, that's a flare gun.

moments.text: Tomer pockets the controller and cracks seeds by the door, in no hurry to leave. Ishai shows him tonight's film on his phone.

lines.say: So tonight, the PixelPlex. What's playing?
A Doll's House. Ibsen. A wife, a secret loan, a door.
A secret loan. That's my uncle's whole life.
It's a classic. Everyone keeps something from someone.
Everyone? Even you?
Me? I can't keep a basil photo from a barista for a week.
Then send it tonight. Or Noa disowns you, and I help her.
After havdalah. I've promised three people already.
Four. And the controller comes back Monday. Probably.
Probably. Like Gadi's payments.
Ouch. Okay. Shavua tov early, habibi.

commentary.say: 'Everyone keeps something from someone.' Tomer just studied his shoes.
'I sat behind her in fourth grade.' Tomer. TOMER. Say more.

update.memory: Took the blue controller. Noa cancelled Ishai's Shabbat dinner too, then sent six exclamation marks. Told him to ask her. Him, not me.

beats.goal: Havdalah at the window, then Ishai finally texts Dana the photo of Moshe and the sprout with one true sentence (Mr. Zelig's): 'He almost died, and now he's showing off.' No 'sorry'. She answers in under a minute, warm. Then a second text: would he ever leave Tel Aviv, for something good? He types and deletes answers and puts the phone face down. He does not ask her why.
beats.teaser: After havdalah, Ishai finally sends Dana the Moshe photo
beats.forceText: After havdalah Ishai sends Dana the photo of Moshe; she answers within a minute.

forceCommentary.say: SENT! Mrs. Levi, Noa, Tomer, Zelig: your boy did it.

moments.text: Three stars over Herzl Street. At the window Ishai lights a candle, holds up a cup of wine and a jar of cloves instead of a spice box; Falafel sniffs the cloves and sneezes.

lines.say: Shavua tov, Falafel. Shavua tov, Moshe. Shavua tov, roommate.
Cloves. Next year a real spice box. Probably.

commentary.say: Three stars, one candle, zero excuses left. The photo, Ishai.
He used cloves. Moshe is offended on behalf of all herbs.

moments.text: At the desk, the photo of Moshe and the sprout on his phone. He types, deletes, types again, reading it out to himself, then sends it and drops the phone like it's hot.

lines.say: 'Sorry it took a wee—' No. Not sorry. 'He almost died, and now he's showing off.'
Send. Sent. Oh no. Sent.

commentary.say: SENT! Mrs. Levi, Noa, Tomer, Zelig: your boy did it.
One true sentence. Mr. Zelig should invoice him.

moments.text: Less than a minute later the phone buzzes. Ishai reads it standing, then again sitting on the bed, Falafel's head on his knee.

message.say: He looks like he's about to ask for a raise. The roommate too. Thank you for remembering. You made my Saturday.

lines.say: Under a minute. She answered in under a minute, Falafel.
'You made my Saturday.' I made someone's Saturday. Me.

commentary.say: 'You made my Saturday.' I am screaming into a cushion.
Under a minute. Faster than Gadi has ever paid anyone.

moments.text: A second text while he is still smiling at the first. The smile goes slowly. He types an answer, deletes it, types another, deletes it, and puts the phone face down next to the notebook.

message.say: Random question. Would you ever leave Tel Aviv? For something good, I mean.

lines.say: 'Would you ever leave Tel Aviv?' Why would she ask that?
'Depends who's...' No. 'Never'? Too much. Later. I'll answer later.

commentary.say: 'Random question.' Babe. Nobody asks that randomly. Nobody.
Somebody's thinking about the future. And it isn't Ishai.

beats.goal: Home after the PixelPlex. An email from Gadi on a Saturday night: Ruti wants the chickpea in Hanukkah colours too, 'small, Monday, we'll settle everything together'. Ishai compares it with the husband in A Doll's House. Then, on the bed, he tries once more to answer Dana's question ('Depends who's asking'), deletes it and turns off the lamp. He goes to sleep with it unanswered.
beats.teaser: Late night: an email from Gadi, and a reply Ishai can't write
beats.forceText: Home after the film, an email from Gadi asks for Hanukkah colours by Monday; Ishai leaves Dana's question unanswered and goes to bed.

forceLines.say: Hanukkah colours. It's November fourteenth, Gadi.

forceCommentary.say: Gadi wants Hanukkah colours, Dana wants an answer. Ishai wants a pillow.

moments.text: Home from the PixelPlex, jacket still on, Falafel's leash still in his hand. The laptop pings: an email from Gadi.

message.say: Shavua tov habibi! Tiny thing: Ruti wants the chickpea in Hanukkah colours too. Small. Monday? We'll settle everything together, promise.

lines.say: Hanukkah colours. It's November fourteenth, Gadi.
'We'll settle everything together.' That's what the husband said in the film. Didn't end well.

commentary.say: Gadi emails on Saturday night like other people breathe.
'Together.' Nora heard that too. Then she bought a ticket.

moments.text: On the edge of the bed with the phone, Dana's question still on the screen. He types 'Depends who's asking', looks at it a long time, deletes it, and turns off the lamp.

lines.say: Tomorrow. In daylight. With coffee. Her coffee.

commentary.say: He deleted the best line he's ever written. I need a minute.
Gadi wants Hanukkah colours, Dana wants an answer. Ishai wants a pillow.

hook.text: Dana asked if he'd ever leave Tel Aviv. Ishai typed three answers and sent none. What will he say, and why did she ask?

previously.text: Noa cancelled Shabbat dinner six minutes before candles. Mrs. Levi brought soup, read his notebook and said: send the photo, not 'sorry'. His thumb stopped over Dana's name.

hosts: Shabbat morning on Herzl Street. Even the buses are resting. Mostly because there aren't any.
Today's to-do list, according to Ishai: walk, rest, send one photo. Mrs. Levi made him promise. So did Noa.
Havdalah tonight at 17:20. After that, no more excuses about the photo.
The Moshe photo has now been 'almost sent' four times. We counted. Oren has a spreadsheet.
Moshe has never looked better. Somebody tell him he's about to be famous.
Mr. Zelig talks to pigeons. The pigeons, I'm told, are very good listeners.
Falafel is the only one in the building with no secrets. Except where the sock went.
Noa cancelled Shabbat dinner six minutes before candles. Two challahs. One Ishai.
Mrs. Levi's cough is still 'the weather'. The weather is sunny and fourteen degrees.
Tonight at nine: the PixelPlex. A Doll's House. A happy home and a secret loan. Sound familiar, Gadi?
If Ishai cries at an Ibsen play tonight, I'm putting it on a T-shirt.
Saturday afternoon in Tel Aviv: half the city asleep, the other half at the beach pretending it's summer.
Dana's been very quiet this week. Quiet people are usually thinking about something big.
Somebody at Cafe Nahat has been looking at train timetables. I'm not saying who. I'm saying trains.
Gadi's last payment date was 'in the system'. Which system, Gadi? The solar system?
Tomer and Noa have known each other since fourth grade. Tomer remembers which desk. Just saying.
Ishai's notebook now has two 'I want's. That's two more than last month.
For new viewers: the basil is Moshe, the dog is Falafel, the man is Ishai, and we are the problem.
Avi's queue is back tonight at half past six. Avi himself, less so.
Shavua tov, everyone. A new week, same apartment, one very nervous thumb.
No votes today, it's Shabbat. Even democracy takes a nap.
Prediction: Ishai deletes his first message to Dana at least twice. Place your bets.
Ishai's walking Falafel past the pond again. The duck has stopped being impressed.
Lior hasn't written a word since Thursday. Writers need Shabbat too. Or material.
radio: Shavua tov from Radio Herzl 88.2! The week starts now, whether you're ready or not.
Buses are back on the road, so if you hear a roar, that's the 88. Be kind to the driver.
Saturday night in Tel Aviv: fourteen degrees, a light wind, perfect for a jacket you'll regret.
Request line's open. Someone wants a song for 'a plant that came back'. Okay, Tel Aviv.
Going to the movies tonight? Bring a sweater. Cinemas are colder than your ex.
The kiosks are opening, the falafel's frying, and the city is pretending tomorrow isn't Sunday.
Here's one for everyone who almost sent a message today. Send it. Or don't. I'm a radio.
News in a minute. First, a song about leaving, because apparently that's our theme tonight.
Dedication from 'apartment five, second floor': for the boy with the tea. That's all it says.
It's late. If you're still up, you're one of us. Turn it down a little, the neighbours sleep.
Herzl Street report: quiet, one dog, one man, one very long text being typed.
Shavua tov again, for those who just woke up from their Shabbat nap. We see you.

zelig: Herzl, you ate already. Don't look at me like that.
Everybody wants a sentence. Nobody wants to wait for it.
1971. A boat. I stayed. The pigeons understand.
The dog counts pigeons. Good. Somebody should.
michal: Saturday run club. Nobody came. Including me.
Who's on treadmill three? I want treadmill three.
sivan: Ten minutes is a warm-up. Twenty is a start.
He'll be back. They always come back on Sunday.
Speed seven. Don't look at speed seven.
lior: Saturday cafes are full of people who aren't writing.
She said December. December is a good chapter title.
kobi: Saturday system: sevens and the birthday of my mother.
Shavua tov! The first one's on... no, it's on you.
The movie people come in after nine. They want to talk about feelings.
After midnight every song is about a woman who left.

street: ...no buses until tonight, so we walk, like our grandparents...
...the kiosk opens after Shabbat, I'll wait...
...she said Haifa is nice, I said so is the sea here...
...Saturday is the only day this street is quiet...
market: ...closed, of course it's closed, it's Saturday...
park: ...my son never visits, but he sends pictures of the dog...
...look at that man talking to the pigeons, every week...
...the duck is a she, everyone says he...
cafe: ...closed till tonight, imagine a city with no coffee...
...shavua tov, a double, please, a double...

chat.say: Shavua tov, neighbours. Reminder: garbage truck Sunday 07:10, bags inside the bins please.
Did anyone hear coughing on the second floor all Shabbat? Is everything ok?
It's the weather. Everybody calm down. Shavua tov.
Stair light is perfect since the electrician fixed it. Tell him thank you from the second floor.
Whose dog was singing at 9 this morning? Very musical. Very early.
Mrs. Levi, the committee bought honey. It's at Moti's. No arguments.
